column1: # wiki_item_locations.tsv -- offline snapshot of each item's wiki.gg |Locations= field.
# Columns (tab-separated): item_id, locations_raw, fetch_date, source_url
# locations_raw is the VERBATIM string from the {{ItemInfobox}} (or, for the
# Vault Key's four tabbed sub-items, the matching NNN_Locations= field) as of
# fetch_date, fetched via `curl -A "blueprince-sim-research/1.0" "<url>?action=raw"`.
# A `!` prefix on an entry marks the wiki's high-luck tier, same convention as
# the wiki page itself. Nothing is filtered, resolved, or excluded here --
# that happens in the checker, not the snapshot. In particular this file
# still contains the non-room mechanic tokens (Experiment, Spiral, Package,
# Trunk, Car Trunk, Dig Spot, Crate, Locker, Dartboard) and the
# already-modelled-elsewhere rooms (Commissary, Locksmith, Lost & Found,
# Trading Post) verbatim, so a future diff can see exactly what the wiki said.
# Scope: one row per special_items.json item whose wiki page carries a real
# |Locations= (or NNN_Locations=) field -- i.e. every item this sweep's spawn
# tables were checked against, plus three fixed-location items (key_8,
# basement_key, master_key) that are Locations=<single value> and are
# deliberately NOT modelled as spawn_rooms (they are guaranteed_in / a shop
# purchase instead -- see each item's meta.notes). Items with no |Locations=
# line at all (Showroom/Armory/Mora Jai Box/Inner Sanctum/Upgrade Disk
# sources, the Sanctum Keys, Cursed Effigy, Royal Scepter -- all fixed or
# puzzle-gated, not floor spawns) are not rows here; there is nothing to
# snapshot for them.
# HONEST LIMIT: this file pins the wiki's stated Locations as of fetch_date.
# It catches SIM DRIFT (special_items.json spawn_rooms silently diverging
# from what this snapshot recorded) but can never catch WIKI DRIFT (the wiki
# itself being edited after fetch_date). Refreshing this snapshot to a later
# wiki revision must be a deliberate, reviewed act with a visible diff, not
# an automatic re-fetch -- a checker that silently re-pulls the wiki on every
# run would defeat the point of pinning a snapshot at all.
# A proposed checker (not wired into tools/validate_data.py -- out of scope
# for this change, another agent owns that file this round):
#   For each row: split locations_raw on ",", strip "!" tier prefixes,
#   drop the fixed non-room-mechanic tokens above, drop entries whose
#   resolved room id is in {commissary, locksmith, lost_and_found,
#   trading_post}, resolve the remainder to rooms.json ids (case-sensitive
#   name match, with the known alias "Spare Servant's Quarters" ->
#   servants_spare_quarters__ix134), and diff the resulting normal/high-luck
#   sets against special_items.json's spawn_rooms/spawn_rooms_high_luck for
#   that item id. Any room present in one set but not the other is a finding
#   (missing = sim under-models the snapshot; extra = sim has a room the
#   snapshot doesn't, which is expected for the Lost & Found/Trading Post/
#   guaranteed_in exceptions noted in each item's meta and should be
#   allow-listed by (item_id, room_id) pair, not silently ignored).
# Necessity guard for each exclusion category (Commissary, Locksmith,
# Lost & Found, Trading Post, and the non-room mechanic tokens): a test that
# temporarily removes the category from the checker's exclusion set and
# asserts the checker THEN reports the pairs it currently suppresses --
# proving the exclusion is load-bearing (the checker would otherwise flag
# those rooms as missing), not merely that the exclusion list still contains
# the expected strings. Concretely, for Lost & Found: assert that with the
# exclusion lifted, the checker flags (gear_wrench, lost_and_found),
# (hall_pass, lost_and_found), (lucky_rabbits_foot, lost_and_found),
# (prism_key, lost_and_found), (repellent, lost_and_found),
# (secret_garden_key, lost_and_found), (stopwatch, lost_and_found),
# (telescope, lost_and_found), (vault_key_370, lost_and_found), and
# (watering_can, lost_and_found) as missing; symmetric tests for Commissary
# (8 pairs), Locksmith (5 pairs), Trading Post (5 pairs), and one test per
# non-room-mechanic token (e.g. lifting the Spiral exclusion should flag
# (car_keys, spiral) et al. as unresolvable, since Spiral has no rooms.json
# id at all -- proving the token is excluded because it doesn't resolve, not
# because the checker forgot to look).
item_id
